data.description:
## Story

As a developer, the cycle-end orchestration has Python building blocks (ledger reader, Jaccard similarity, cycle dispatcher) that decide when to halt, re-cycle, or dispatch the arbiter, so that the cycle-K logic in REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md Step 4.75 is implementable as executable code (not just prose).

## Done Definitions

- [ ] New module `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/cycle_ledger.py` with `read_ledger(path) -> dict`, `write_ledger(path, ledger)`, `append_cycle(path, cycle_num, findings_tuples, commit_sha, findings_hash, halt_reason=None)`, `reconstruct_from_pr_comments(pr_number, repo) -> dict`. Atomic writes via the lock pattern used by write-cycle-ledger.sh; same lock file used to coordinate with the shell writer.
- [ ] Cycle ledger schema extended (cycle-ledger.md contract updated): each cycle entry now contains `findings` (array of [file, line_range, category] tuples), `commit_sha` (40-char string), and optional `reconstruction_gaps` (boolean). schema_version bumped 1.0.0 → 1.1.0 with backward-compat reader handling absent fields.
- [ ] PR comment marker format extended: `DSO-Review-Cycle: K commit_sha=<sha> findings_hash=<h> tuples=<json>` where tuples is a JSON array of [file, line_range, category] entries. Format documented in cycle-ledger.md. Reconstruction parser extracts all fields and tolerates malformed lines (logs warning, skips entry).
- [ ] New module `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/stability.py` with `finding_hash(tuple_dict) -> str` (stable hash of file+line_range+category), `jaccard(set_a, set_b) -> float` (zero-set edge case returns 1.0), `should_halt(current, prior, threshold=0.85) -> tuple[bool, str|None]`. Jaccard inputs are POST-RESOLUTION findings (what remains in reviewer-findings.json after resolution loop completes).
- [ ] New module `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/cycle_dispatcher.py` with `next_action(ledger, max_cycles, current_findings, current_commit_sha) -> dict` returning `{"action": "PASS"|"DISPATCH_NEXT"|"DISPATCH_ARBITER"|"SHORT_CIRCUIT", "reason": str, "cycle_num": int}`.
- [ ] cycle_dispatcher handles all edge cases from scenario walkthrough: (a) SHORT_CIRCUIT when current commit_sha matches last cycle and arbiter-rulings.json already exists for that SHA; (b) reset cycle_num to 1 when current SHA differs from last cycle SHA (local re-run after user fix); (c) skip Jaccard for cycle 1 (no prior); (d) skip Jaccard when prior cycle has reconstruction_gaps=true; (e) PASS on UNRESOLVED==0; (f) DISPATCH_ARBITER on cycle_num >= max_cycles with unresolved findings; (g) DISPATCH_ARBITER on STABLE_HALT with unresolved critical/important findings; (h) DISPATCH_NEXT otherwise.
- [ ] Unit tests for each module: ≥85% branch coverage; explicit tests for each edge case in DD6; tests for atomic-write contention and reconstruction parser tolerance.

## Considerations

- [Dual-mode] Reader works locally (read $ARTIFACTS_DIR/cycle-ledger.json) and in CI (reconstruct from PR comments via `gh api`). Same Python API, two entry points.
- [Schema evolution] schema_version bumped 1.0.0 → 1.1.0; readers handle absent fields (forward+backward compat). cycle-ledger.md contract updated atomically.
- [Atomic writes] Reuse the lock from S2 (`write-cycle-ledger.sh`); coordinate via the same lock file when Python writes. Don't introduce new locking primitives.
- [Dependency boundary] This story produces modules; it does NOT wire them into runner.py or /dso:commit. Wiring is Stories 13 and 14.
- [Escalation policy] Escalate when blocked.
